thread:
incident-bot: PAGING: hosted-runtime kvcache shard memory surge -> OOMs. Observed sudden kvcache growth correlated with batch-config canary (batch-window v1.9). Elevated 500s on generation endpoints. @oncall-ryan please respond :rotating_light:

oncall-ryan: Ack. I’m looking now. Any tracer logs or top offenders?

eva-sre: Seeing KVCacheMap size jump on shard-7, prefix cardinality spiked. Continuous-batching config change widened window and increased prefetch depth.

sam-support: Multiple customers reporting 500s for long-prompt workloads starting 13:21 UTC. First ticket from internal QA flagged at 13:23.

oncall-ryan: Triage plan: 1) pause canary rollout 2) revert batch-window change in control plane 3) apply prefetch throttle on hosted runtime 4) enable smaller-model fallback for affected routes 5) increase eviction aggressiveness temporarily. Executing step 1.

ops-lee: On it — pausing canary now.

```bash
# pause canary daemonset
kubectl -n runtime rollout pause ds/kvcache-canary
# quick revert API (control plane)
curl -XPOST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/changes/revert -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"change_id":"batch-window-v1.9"}'
```

deploy-bot: revert job queued (job-id: revert-7744). Canary pause acknowledged.

oncall-ryan: Applying prefetch throttle to hosted runtime traffic path. Will reduce prefetch depth from 6 -> 2 and cap max_context_tokens to 32k for affected pools.

ops-lee: Patch applied to hosted-config: prefetch_depth=2, max_context_tokens=32000.

```yaml
# hosted runtime patch (applied)
route: /v1/generate
prefetch:
  depth: 2
  enabled: true
context:
  max_tokens: 32000
continuous_batching:
  max_batch_size: 64  # temporarily lowered
```

eva-sre: After throttle, shard-7 memory is trending down. KVCacheMap growth rate reduced ~75% over 4 minutes. CPU and latency stable.

sam-support: Customer-facing impact reduced; number of 500s dropped to near baseline. I’ll hold on comms until we confirm rollback success.

oncall-ryan: Rollback job completed per deploy-bot. Canary revert done, full rollout paused. Still keeping prefetch throttle until we validate canary changes in staging and run a focused perf regression.

product-amy: Noted. Preparing a short customer note for affected tenants explaining mitigation and next steps. ETA 25m.

oncall-ryan: Root cause hypothesis: the batch-window change increased continuous-batching prefix expansion and prefetching which amplified prefix cardinality for long prompts -> KV map churn -> OOM on hot shards. We'll run a targeted repro and add a safety cap to prefetch when prefix-cardinality metric spikes.

ops-lee: Putting quick guard in place: if kvcache_map_growth_rate > 1000/s then disable prefetch for that shard. I’ll add to runtime circuit-breakers.

deploy-bot: circuit-breaker rule applied to prod runtime (rule-id cb-921).

oncall-ryan: Customer impact assessment: ~4 customers had >5% error rate spike for ~8 minutes. No data loss. We'll reach out to top-affected accounts.

sam-support: I opened incident tickets for the 4 tenants and assigned follow-ups.

product-amy: Draft ready, sharing in #customer-comms for review.

oncall-ryan: Handoff to night oncall @marco-plat in 30m. Current state: memory trending down, revert complete, prefetch throttle & circuit-breaker active, monitoring dashboards and alerts tuned to kvcache_map_growth_rate and prefetch activity. Please escalate if errors reoccurs.

marco-plat: Ack, taking handoff. I’ll keep the throttle in place and validate the scheduled regression run tomorrow.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, customer impact reduced. Follow-up items: postmortem RCA, safe prefetch threshold, regression test in staging.

oncall-ryan: Adding notes to incident runbook and pinging research to help with quantization/rebalancing recommendations. Closing active pager. :white_check_mark:
